headline: Continual AutoResearch finds persistent state speeds early research, but does not reliably improve final results
summary: A 3 November 2026 preprint introduces Continual AutoResearch, a matched benchmark for comparing persistent and reset AI agents across nine machine-learning task families. The authors report that persistent state improved fixed-budget search efficiency for all five evaluated CLI agents, mainly by producing a valid solution sooner or a stronger first solution. Final held-out performance was much less consistent: only Sonnet 4.6 showed a substantial aggregate outcome gain, and most agents lost their efficiency advantage after controls for first-solution latency and candidate count. An explicit memory ablation and trace cases show that relevant prior insights can improve initialization, while overly specific prior state can anchor search and yield worse final selections. These are author-reported results from short task streams; the paper says its code will be released with the camera-ready version.
